_readme: Opponent matchup notes for the printable packet (scouting report page). Authored in Claude sessions and committed — the Hub only renders. Per team: storylines = [{h:'HEADLINE',b:'one- or two-sentence body'}] printed under '<OPP> Storylines'; series_note = optional caveat printed in small italics under the storylines (data flags, scheduling quirks). Empty entries render '— storylines to come —'. Never invent a number here; anything uncertain carries its flag in the text.

storylines.b: Game 1 opens Pee Dee's SPHL era at the Florence Center — and the first Havoc–IceCats game ever played. Pro hockey returns to Florence, where the ECHL's Pee Dee Pride played 1997–2005.

storylines.h: THE CARDIAC CATS ARRIVE — 2025-26 WAS FPHL
storylines.b: Their only Florence season: 24-25-2-5, 4th in the FPHL's Continental Division — then a nine-game playoff run: swept top-seed Athens 2-0 despite going 3-11 against them, took Columbus in two overtime thrillers, and lost the Commissioner's Cup Final 3-1 to Binghamton. Every number from last year is FPHL, not SPHL.
Pee Dee set the FPHL single-season attendance record (126,841 — 4,698 a night) and the single-game record (7,837 vs Athens, Jan 17, 2026). Home playoff White Outs became the identity.

storylines.h: A NEW ERA BEHIND THE BENCH
storylines.b: Chris Bernard takes his first professional head-coaching job for the SPHL debut; GM Tom Callahan doubles as the team's broadcaster. Coach Gary Graham retired after the Cup final.

Per Elite Prospects — confirm before air: goalie Parker Rutherford and defenseman Charlie Bedard return for the SPHL season; leading scorer Patriks Marcinkevics (42-48—90, FPHL) headlined the Florence year, and Houston Wilson (18-41—59) departed to Port Huron.

Pee Dee IceCats.series_note: First SPHL meeting — no prior series between the clubs in any league. All 2025-26 Pee Dee figures in these notes are FPHL and never compare side-by-side with SPHL numbers.

storylines.h: ONE GAME. ONE DRESS REHEARSAL. THEN IT COUNTS.
storylines.b: The Oct 9 exhibition is the only preseason game either club plays — the single dress rehearsal before both open for real. Watch what each bench is trying to learn: new faces in top-six minutes, fresh defensive pairs, and how the goalie workload splits.

storylines.h: TWO FIRST-ROUND EXITS, ONE FRESH START
storylines.b: Both teams left last spring early: Huntsville finished 2nd (32-20-5-1, 70 points) and was upset in round 1 by #7 Knoxville; Pensacola finished 5th (28-21-6-3, 65) and fell 1-2 in round 1 to eventual champion Evansville. Both enter 2026-27 trying to move past an early postseason ending.

storylines.h: LAST YEAR'S SERIES BELONGED TO HUNTSVILLE — WITH ONE UGLY NIGHT
storylines.b: The Havoc took the 2025-26 season series 5-2-1 and outscored Pensacola 32-24, including 6-2, 7-1 and 7-3 statements at Propst — but Pensacola answered with an 8-1 hammering in Pensacola on Nov 26. The series swings hard both ways.
Dawson Sciarrino split 2025-26 between these clubs — 34 games for Pensacola (6-9—15), then 14 down the stretch for Huntsville (4-9—13). First look at the team that traded him away.

storylines.h: A FOUR-CUP FRANCHISE UNDER JEREMY GATES
storylines.b: Pensacola's four Presidents Cups are the measuring stick in this rivalry — Huntsville leads the all-time series 72-37-14 across 123 games, with the playoff ledger even at two series apiece.

Pensacola Ice Flyers.series_note: 2025-26 season series (from the committed league log): Huntsville 5-2-1 — 3-1-0 at home, 2-1-1 on the road, 32 GF / 24 GA across 8 meetings.
